(15)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Question 17 of the Application for Degrees of Masonry
was amended in 1953 to include, in addition to the one year waiting
period, the requirement that newly raised Master Masons be proficient in
the Candidate's Lecture of the Master Mason Degree before applying for,
or receiving any degree, or being initiated in any Lodge, Order or Organization, the prerequisite of membership wherein is that a person be a
Master Mason; and
WHEREAS, it was believed that such requirement of proficiency in the
Candidate's Lecture of the Master Mason Degree would cause the newly
raised Brethren to attend Lodge and become active in Lodge affairs; and
WHEREAS, surveys show that the requirement of such proficiency is
not causing newly raised Brethren to attend Lodge or participate in Lodge
activities and therefore has not served its intended purpose; and
WHEREAS, this requirement of such proficiency has created a double
standard of pre-1953 and post-1953 Master Masons and is unfairly hindering many new Master Masons from seeking further light in Masonry
which can be beneficial to Blue Lodges; and
WHEREAS, the day to day living and practice of the tenets of Freemasonry come from within the heart, soul and character of the Mason and
not from his capabilities of memorizing; and
WHEREAS, the newly raised Brother is congratulated by the Worshipful Master and informed that nothing now remains to constitute him a
member of the Lodge, but to approach the Secretary's table and sign the
by-laws, which will subject him to its burdens and responsibilities, as well
as entitle him to its benefits and its privileges; and
WHEREAS, the retention of the one year delay before receiving any
degree or being initiated in any organization the prerequisite of membership wherein is that a person be a Master Mason, affords sufficient time
and opportunity for a new Master Mason to gain information, become
familiar with the spirit of his Lodge, become proficient in the Candidate's
Lecture of the Master Mason Degree, and become an active member of
his Lodge.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that Question 17 of the
Application for Degrees be amended to read:
"Do you promise that you will not apply for, or receive any degree, or
be initiated in any Lodge, Order, or Organization, the prerequisite of
membership wherein is that a person be a Master Mason, within twelve
months after you have received the Degree of Master Mason?"
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Section 2635 of the California
Masonic Code be amended and that all other necessary additions, revisions, deletions or amendments be effected to revise the Code to comply
with the intent of this Resolution.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes (Majority Report):
Resolution No. 15 would delete from Question No. 17 on the Application for Degrees, an applicant's promise not to apply for. degr~es in
prerequisite bodies until he had exhibited the necessary proficiency m the
Candidate's Lecture of the Third Degree.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes believes that one
method of developing a mature Master Mason is by encouraging his

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

personal attention and effort to learning portions of the ritual he has
witnessed. A knowledgeable instructor or coach who teaches the Candidate's Lecture is an invaluable ingredient in this maturation. We would
not wish to take any action which could be interpreted in any manner
other than to encourage this process and person-to-person contact.
The purpose of our ritual is to impart certain moral truths in an innovative form. We should ask ourselves, what useful purpose is to be served
by any reduction of ritual? Proficiency in the Candidate's Lectures is an
additional means of teaching the fundamentals of Freemasonry.
Researching the information available when this proficiency requirement was adopted in 1953 reveals no intent to deprive concordant bodies
of potential members. Rather, the intent was to improve the opportunities
for Master Masons to become better versed in the foundations of the
Fraternity. Further, there is no evidence that this requirement has been a
serious deterrent to membership in concordant bodies.
Finally, the proponents of Resolution No. 15 state that the proficiency
requirement has created a double standard in that there are pre-1953 and
post-1953 Masons. This argument is specious for if we are to consider
every change as creating a double standard, we could never amend or
create any of our laws and regulations, for on that basis it could be argued
that even an increase in the fees for degrees would create a double
standard.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes concludes, therefore,
that the best interests of Freemasonry can be served by allowing the law
to remain as it is.
We recommend a "NO" vote on Resolution No. 15.

Prior to 1978 a Master Mason could be elected, installed and serve as
Worshipful Master of a Lodge in this Jurisdiction without his having taken
a Third Degree proficiency. If this was permitted, why shouldn't the same
Master Mason be permitted to seek membership in a Concordant Masonic
Organization? Is it fair for Grand Lodge to permit one and deny the
other? It appears that the law is inconsistant in its application.
This Resolution does not eliminate the required one year waiting period.
It merely deletes the present required Third Degree proficiency.
The teachings of Masonry and the communication of the principles
thereof are not solely dependent upon the memorization of words. Masonry comes from within the heart and is the understanding about Masonic
tenets which the individual receives from the three degrees as well as how
he lives and carries out those principles.
We offer this minority report, not to aid or assist any of the Concordant
Masonic Organizations, but in the sincere belief that each Master Mason
should be treated equally.
The undersigned members of the Policy and General Purposes Committee recommend a "YES" vote on Resolution No. 15.

existence until 1953. In that year Grand Lodge adopted legislation requiring every Master Mason to pass a proficiency in the Third Degree if
he desired membership in a Concordant Masonic Organization. This legislation established two so-called "classes" of Master Masons:

Immediately after an application for the degrees of Masonry or for
membership by affiliation is received by a Lodge, the Lodge Secretary
shall transmit to the Grand Secretary the name, date of birth and current
address of the Applicant.
The Grand Secretary shall check his list and record of expulsions,
suspensions, rejections and restorations, and within ten (10) days after his
receipt of the name, date of birth and current address of an Applicant for
the degrees of Masonry or for membership by affiliation, report his findings to the Lodge Secretary.
No ballot shall be taken on an application for the degrees of Masonry
or for membership by affiliation until the Grand Secretary's findings, as
specified above, have been announced at the Stated Meeting at which the
ballot is to be taken."
RESOLVED further that Section 1108-lOth of the California Masonic
Code be amended to read as follows:
"10th. To keep in his office a full and complete list and record of all
expulsions, suspensions, rejections and restorations of which he shall be
notified by the several Lodges and when requested by a Lodge Secretary
to check this list and record and to report his findings to the requesting
Lodge Secretary within ten (10) days of receipt of the request, in accordance with this Code."
RESOLVED further that this legislation shall become operative law on
July 1 of the calendar year after adoption.
Because the proponents of this Resolution amended it as specified
above, and the amended Resolution was not received by the Grand Secretary at least 90 days prior to the commencement of this Grand Lodge
Communication, it must be considered as emergent legislation pursuant
to Section 160 of the California Masonic Code.
To bring the matter before this Communication, we therefore move that
the proposed legislation be considered at this time by this Grand Lodge
as emergent legislation. To carry, this motion requires a 516 vote.
Failing to receive the required 516 affirmative vote to be considered as
emergent legislation, the proponents withdrew the Resolution.

WAIVE INITIATION FEES-CERTAIN DEMOLAYS

RESOLVED, that Section 3 be added to Section 2086, Article VIII of
the California Masonic Code to read as follows:

(17)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, statistics from this Grand Jurisdiction show that for the
past several years membership in the Craft has been rapidly declining; and
WHEREAS, the average age of a Mason in this Grand Jurisdiction is
over the age of forty-nine (49) years; and
WHEREAS, the age of applicants for the degrees of Masonry in this
Grand Jurisdiction is seldom under the age of thirty (30); and
WHEREAS, the Order of DeMolay has a vast untapped source of
potential Masons possessing leadership and ritualistic qualities; and
WHEREAS, when a DeMolay first becomes eligible to apply for the
degrees of Masonry he is at a period in his life when our initiation fees
could be a financial hardship.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the California Masonic
Code be ammended to allow any Masonic Lodge under this Grand Jurisdiction, by a vote of the Lodge to waive the initiation fees if the applicant
meets the following criteria:
A. That he be over twenty-one (21) years of age, and has not reached
his twenty-second (22) birthday on the date of application, and
B. That he be a Past Master Councilor of a DeMolay Chapter chartered
by the International Supreme Council Order of DeMolay whose
See is at Kansas City, in the State of Missouri.
Respectfully submitted,
LAWRENCE C. THOMPSON, M No. 523
L. LAWRENCE BAIRD, SW No. 523 JAMES B. ALLEN, PM No. 523

Referred to the Committees on Jurisprudence and Policy and General
Purposes:

The Committee on Jurisprudence:
The Committee on Jurisprudence to which this Resolution has been
referred, reports as follows:
This Resolution proposes to allow any Lodge to waive the initiation
fees for DeMolay Past Master Councilors who are 21 years of age. The
proponents seek to allow waiver only of the initiation fees and thus each
Lodge would still pay the required sum pursuant to Section 1704 for every
degree it shall confer, and each applicant for the degrees would still be
requ.ired to accompany his petition with the contribution pursuant to
Section 1706 for the use and benefit of the Masonic Homes of California
and the required sums pursuant to Section 1712 for the Endowment Fund
of the George Washington Masonic National Memorial and for the use
and benefit of the California Masonic Memorial Temple.
To carry out the intent of the proponents, your Committee submits the
following:

"Section 3. Sections 1 and 2 of this Article VIII shall not apply to a
Past Master Councilor of a DeMolay Chapter chartered by the International Supreme Council Order of DeMolay, and no fees for degrees
shall be payable by such person, provided that on the date the Lodge
receives the application for degrees such person shall then be twentyone years of age and not have attained the age of twenty-two and th.e
Lodge, by majority vote of the members present on the date the apphcation is received, waives the fee."
RESOLVED further, that the first sentence of Section 2684 be amended
to read as follows:
"Except as authorized by Section 2086, Article VIII, Section 2 of this
Code, a Lodge shall not confer a degree gratuitously, nor donate a fee
back to an applicant under any pretext whatever."
RESOLVED further, that Section 2686 of the California Masonic Code
be amended by inserting after "case," in the third line on Page 182 the
words, "except as to fees waived by Section 2086, Article VIII, Section
3 of this Code."
To place the matter before Grand Lodge, we move the adoption of the
Resolution.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution No. 17 proposes to amend Section 2684 CMC to permit, by
vote of a Constituent Lodge, to waive the initiation fees if the applicant
meets the following· two requirements:
A. That he be over twenty-one (21) years of age, and has not reached
his twenty-second (22) birthday on the date of application, and,
B. That he be a Past Master Councilor of a DeMolay Chapter chartered
by the International Supreme Council Order of DeMolay.
This Resolution proposes to establish preferential treatment within the
membership of the Order of DeMolay and create two classes of applicants
which is contrary to Masonic principles and the policy of this Grand Lodge
and discriminates against all DeMolays who are not Past Master Councilors.
We all respect and hold in high esteem those who have served their
DeMolay Chapter as Master Councilors however, it is the opinion of your
Committee on Policy and General Purposes that no economic distinction
should be made among applicants from the Order of DeMolay.
Your Committee must point out that this Resolution does not provide
for the $25.00 Masonic Homes contribution fee, the present $1.00 George
Washington National Memorial fee or the $9.00 fee for the use and benefit
of the California Masonic Memorial Temple required of all applicants in
this Jurisdiction under Section 2686 and Section 1712 CMC.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a "NO"
vote.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

The Committee on Youth Orders:
While Resolution No. 17 was not referred to this Committee, the comments applied to Resolution No. 13 also apply to this Resolution.
Resolution No. 17 would establish special privileges for members of the
Order of DeMolay insofar as qualifications for the degrees of Masonry
are concerned. If adopted, this Resolution would, in effect, create two
classes of Masons: those who are Senior DeMolays, and those who are
not. It is felt very strongly that preferential consideration for Senior
DeMolays in connection with becoming members of a Masonic Lodge is
not in the best interests of either the Masonic Fraternity or the Order of
DeMolay; and, in fact, would be inconsistent with the precepts of both .
A "NO" vote is recommended.

The Committee on Jurisprudence:
The Committee on Jurisprudence, to which Resolution No. 19 has been
referred, reports as follows:
. .
Masonic law now provides that an amendment to the Constitution and
Ordinances of Grand Lodge, if not approved by a 516 vote in the year
when presented, but receives a majority vote, shall carry over to the next
year, and then may be adopted by a 2/3 vote. This Resolution, applying
to Ordinances only, would permit an amendment to be adopted. the first
year by a 2/3 vote only, and eliminates any carry-over. .
.
To carry out the intent of the proponent, your Committee submits the
following:
.
.
.
.
RESOLVED, that Section 4002 of the Cahfornia Masonic Code is
amended to read as follows:

264

Not Adopted.

REDUCE REQUIRED VOTE AND DELETE CARRY OVER
PROVISIONS FOR AMENDING C.M.C.
(19)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Section 4002 of the C.M.C. requires a five-sixths favorable
vote of the members present at an Annual Communication to pass or
amend any of the Ordinances; and
WHEREAS, Section 4004 of the C.M.C. provides that if a proposed
amendment receives more than a majority vote but less than the fivesixths required for its adoption, it shall lie over for one year to the next
Annual Communication at which time a two-thirds vote shall be sufficient
for its adoption; and
WHEREAS, it is extremely difficult to pass or amend an Ordinance
under the present requirement of five-sixths of the votes of an Annual
Communication; and
WHEREAS, many financial, moral and practical detriments result from
proposed amendments lying over for one year; and
WHEREAS, reducing the required vote from five-sixths to two-thirds
and deleting the provision for carry over would not only provide a desirable flexibility but would also maintain a sound and reasonable stability.
NOW, THEREFORE , BE IT RESOLVED that Section 4002 of the
C.M.C. be amended to substitute two-thirds for five-sixths.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Section 4004 of the C.M.C. be
deleted.
Respectfully submitted,
EDWARD E. SEAGLE, PM No. 730

Referred to the Committees on Jurisprudence and Policy and General
Purposes.

"VOTE REQUIRED: Upon the report of said Committee, if two-thirds
of the vote shall be in favor of such proposed amendment, it shall be
declared adopted; and, from and after the close of that Communication,
it shall become a part of these Ordinances."
RESOLVED FURTHER, that Section 4004 of the California Masonic
Code is hereby repealed.
.
. .
To place this matter before Grand Lodge, we move the adoption ot this
resolution.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
This Resolution would eliminate the 5/6 vote required at present for
amending our law.
Benjamin Franklin once wrote: "For when you assemble a number of
men to have the advantage of their joint wisdom, you .inevitably ass~~ble
with those men all their prejudices, their passions, the1r errors of opinion,
their local interests and their selfish views. From such an Assembly can
a perfect production be expected?"
.
.
.
The Founding Fathers of our Fraternity recognized the. importance ~f
virtual unanimity of opinion in our regulations. A unanimous ballot •.s
required for admission to a Lodge to ensure that harmony shall p~evail
and that all can work together for the common purpose of creating a
universal brotherhood. So the body of law which governs us is adopted
by a nearly unanimous accord. We provide protectio~ for t~e majorit~ by
requiring a lapse of time - one year - before recons1derat1on to achieve
passage of the change by a lesser vote (two-thirds).
.
No financial nor moral harm has resulted from caut10n, the lapse of
time and a further review of judgment and wisdom.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a "NO"
vote.
Not Adopted.

EMERGENT RESOLUTION- GEORGE WASHINGTON
MASONIC NATIONAL MEMORIAL CONTRIBUTIONS

To bring the matter before this Communication, we therefore move that
the proposed legislation be considered at this time by this Grand Lodge
as emergent legislation.
Since this Grand Lodge voted to consider the matter at this time, to
place the legislation before you, we move the adoption of the Resolution.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, George Washington led our forefathers to independence
and was a leader in founding the United States of America where we are
privileged to live today and was our first President, and
WHEREAS, George Washington served as Master of his Masonic
Lodge, laid the cornerstone of our National Capitol, and performed many
other Masonic duties to the glory of our Fraternity, and
WHEREAS, the Masons of the United States of America caused a
beautiful building to be erected in Alexandria, Virginia as a Memorial to
The Father of Our Country and to house the historical documents and
Masonic property associated with George Washington, and to serve as a
Museum for all to see and admire, and
WHEREAS, this beautiful building has been maintained by the Masons
of the United States and in California by a contribution of $1.00 by each
candidate for the Degrees of Masonry, but in recent years inflation made
these Masonic contributions insufficient to properly care for the great
Memorial and a majority of the Grand Lodges have increased their contributions and others are planning to do so as they gather for their Annual
Communications.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 1712 of the
California Masonic Code be amended to increase the contributions by
each candidate to this Memorial from $1.00 to $5.00 so that the Grand
Lodge of California may join in this program to protect and maintain the
George Washington Masonic National Memorial.

Respectfully submitted,
H. DOUGLAS LEMONS, PM No. 699
Referred to the Committees on Jurisprudence and Policy and General
Purposes.
The Committee on Jurisprudence:
Your Committee on Jurisprudence, to which the Resolution to increase
fees payable by applicants for contribution to the George Washington
Masonic National Memorial was referred, reports as follows:
To carry out the intent of the proponent, we move the adoption of the
following Resolution:
RESOLVED, that Section 1712 of the California Masonic Code be
amended by substituting in the third line on page 88, the words "five
dollars" for the words "one dollar."
Since this proposed legislation was not presented to the Grand Secretary
at least 90 days prior to the commencement of this Annual Communication, it must be considered as emergent legislation pursuant to Section 160
of the California Masonic Code.

267

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
This Resolution would increase the initiation fee by increasing from $1.00
to $5.00 the candidate's contribution to the George Washington Masonic
National Memorial.
The Memorial honors one of America's most notable Masons. Inflation
must affect its maintenance as it affects all of us. If past contributions truly
have been insufficient, an increase is warranted to make the Memorial a
proper showcase.
We recommend a "YES" vote.

Adopted-5/6 vote.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
Your Committee on Finance is pleased to submit its report for the 197980 Grand Lodge year.
Financial reports relating to the Grand Lodge which are included in the
Grand Treasurer's report reveal that total costs to operate your Grand
Lodge during the past fiscal year increased slightly more than twelve
percent (12% ), a relatively modest increase in the light of current conditions. We note an appreciable increase in the cost of our insurance and
are hopeful that a review of our insurance program can be accomplished
during the next fiscal year.
The necessary supplemental appropriations for those items where budgets were exceed, totaled $75,300, which were duly approved by the Grand
Master. It is well to note that half of that amount is represented by two
major items, public liability insurance for Lodges, and Constituent Lodge
supplies, the latter being an inventory item from which offsetting income
will be received, as sold. Very few Committees exceeded their budget,
and we congratulate the Committee Chairmen for their diligent control.
We have reviewed the Grand Master's report and the Grand Treasurer's
report and concur in actions taken.
The publication and distribution of our California Freemason Magazine
for the 1980-81 year is estimated to cost $140,000. We believe that this
magazine is .most meaningful and of great benefit to the Craft; a per capita
assessment increase of $ .10 will be included in our final motion.
With the continuing growth of the Endowment Fund along with a
business oriented administration, the Homes have been operating within
these funds. This has included for a number of years a per capita charge
of $1.00 per member. We are happy to note that the Board of Trustees
has recommended the discontinuance of the $1.00 per capita charge for
the coming fiscal year; we are pleased to concur.
.Your <;ommittee on Finance has again concluded that for purposes of
re1mbursmg Grand Lodge Officers, staff, Committeemen, Inspectors, etc.
for the use of their personal cars on Grand Lodge business, fixed costs
should not be included. After careful review and evaluation of current
data, we considered the adequacy of reimbursement rates as they would
apply to those few individuals who regularly drive their personal cars
several thousand miles a year on Grand Lodge business, as well as to
those who occasionally use their personal automobiles to travel a few
miles on behalf of Grand Lodge. Accordingly, the rate of reimbursement
for the use of personal vehicles on Grand Lodge business from the close
of this Annual Communication until the corresponding date in 1981 is set
at $ .18 per mile.
The ne~ Grand Lodge data processing system is currently being installed usmg a planned phase approach, which will allow its estimated
total cost of $75,000 to be funded over a period of three years.
Duri~g the coming year the system will provide Grand Lodge the ability
to monitor and control their accounting and financial functions more

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

269

effectively and efficiently at a budgeted cost of $25,000, thereby fulfilling
an immediate need while maintaining the cost each year to Grand Lodge
at a reasonable level. The system will also be expanded in the future to
replace several manual systems currently in use resulting in increased
savings in labor costs.
We have enjoyed the wise and helpful counsel of Very Worshipful John
A. Sickenberger, Grand Treasurer, during the past year, and wish to offer
our thanks for his expert and concerned attention to the financial affairs
of the Grand Lodge and his close cooperation with the Committee on
Finance, to which he has additionally served as Consultant.
We are grateful to Very Worshipful Verne Hendrix, Grand Secretary,
and his staff who have given your Committee so much cheerful assistance
whenever we called upon them.
The 1980-81 proposed budget, which is here presented, was reviewed
in detail with the Elective Line, the Grand Treasurer and the Grand
Secretary.
Details of the budget will be published in the Proceedings. A summary
is as follows:

In addition to the above appointments, the Grand Master-elect announced the following appointments:
To serve as Trustees of the Masonic Homes of California, the reappointment of Kermit A. Jacobson, Stephen J. Collins, Raymond A. Ebbage,
John M. Palmer, Jr., Ralph Hinds and Hambleton F. Leas; and the appointment of Chester R. MacPhee, Ronald A. Sherod and Ronald D.
Waddell.
NOTE: Following the installation of the Grand Lodge Officers, it was
reported that R:.W:. Robert 0. West, Deputy Grand Master; R:.W:.
Harry L. Maynard, Senior Grand Warden, and R:.W:. E. Arthur Haglund, Junior Grand Warden, by virtue of their respective offices, are also
members of the Masonic Homes of California Board of Trustees.
It was further reported that R:.W:. Robert 0. West was appointed a
Trustee of the California Masonic Memorial Temple in lieu of H. Douglas
Lemons and that Harold S. Stein, Mark E. Schrock, Leonard Freeland
and Stanley M. Cazneaux were reappointed as Trustees. The appointment
of Sam M. Pavlovich and James I. Mendenhall completed the required
number of Trustees.
At 11:45 A.M. Grand Lodge was called off for the purpose of installing
the Grand Lodge Officers elected and appointed for the ensuing year. It
was announced that the installation would be an "open" one and would
commence at 2:00 P.M.

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
At 2:00 P.M. the Installation Ceremony commenced, with the retiring
Grand Master, Most Worshipful Vernon L. Gordon, acting as Installing
Officer, and Past Grand Master Kermit A. Jacobson acting as Master of
Ceremonies. In accordance with the Ritual, all of the Appointive Officers
were duly installed after which the Grand Lecturer, Grand Secretary and
Grand Treasurer were installed. The Junior Grand Warden and Senior
Grand Warden were then invested with the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins
and appropriately installed in their respective stations. The Deputy Grand
Master was presented with the lapel pin of his office and installed after
which the Grand Master was duly installed. Grand Master Lemons expressed his appreciation to the installing "team" and invited each of the
Elective Officers to introduce those members of their families who were
in attendance.
The newly installed Grand Master then requested the Grand Marshal
to present the wife of the Junior Past Grand Master, Mae Gordon, in the

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

275

East, and called upon the Grand Treasurer who graciously presented her
with a gift on behalf of the entire membership of the Fraternity. This
charming lady then eloquently responded in expressing her appreciation.
Maxine Lemons, the wife of Grand Master Lemons, was escorted to
the altar and presented with a beautiful boquet of flowers for which she
appropriately expressed her thanks.
Past Grand Master Kermit A. Jacobson presented to the Junior Past
Grand Master, the Past Grand Master's apron. Past Grand Master and
Past Grand Secretary, Edward H. Siems, then presented the Grand Master's lapel pin to the retiring Grand Master, following which he was presented with the Past Grand Master's Certificate by Past Grand Master
Eugene S. Hopp. Each of these presentations were made with expressions
of gratitude on behalf of the Masons of this Jurisdiction.
The Grand Master then asked the residents of the Masonic Homes who
were present to stand for recognition. He then presented the Master and
the Brethren of his Lodge who had journeyed from Long Beach to be in
attendance at his installation. Also presented were the Long Beach Masters of 1966 which was the year the Grand Master served as Master of his
Lodge. Grand Master Lemons introduced some of his business associates,
following which members of his family were introduced. His two lovely
daughters approached the East and thrilled their father by presenting to
him a gavel. Assistant Grand Lecturer, Morton B. Glick, on behalf of the
Long Beach Masters of 1966 presented to the Grand Master a handsome
gold Grand Master's Jewel.
Grand Master Lemons then addressed those assembled. He commented
that he was the first Grand Master ever from the Long Beach area and
how proud and joyous he was at this singular honor. He further commented that there is much to do in the job ahead, that certain changes
must be made in the light of changing times. He indicated several areas
that need addressing; Masonic Education, leadership education, communication and cooperation with the general public and strengthening the
bonds of brotherhood within the Fraternity. He concluded his remarks by
outlining some of his programs for the forthcoming year and reminded
those assembled that by working together we shall prove to all that
Masonry is an instrument of unity which will become a splendid monument
to accomplishment upon which the world will gaze with admiration.
At the conclusion of the Grand Master's challenging address he was
accorded a standing ovation.
The Benediction was delivered by the newly installed Grand Chaplain,
and all business of the 131st Annual Communication being completed at
3:30 P.M., a reception for the newly installed Officers was then given,
following which Grand Lodge was closed at 4:30 P.M.

NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
The financial statements of 'nle Most Worshipf;.l Grand Lodge of
Free and Accepted Masons of the State of C&lifornia have been prepared
on the accrual basis of accounting. Significant accounting policies
follow:
Furniture, Equipment and Improvements:
REPORT OF CERTIFIED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANTS

Additions and betterments to property are capitalized at cost
and are not depreciated. Expenditures which represent maintenance and
repairs are charged to expense. The property accounts are relieved of
cost upon disposition.

NOTE 2 - PENSION PLAN
The Grand Lodge contributes to the California Masonic Retirement
Plan for the benefit of all eligible full-ti.me employees, Total pension
expense for the years enaed June 30, 1980 and 1979 was $12,644 and $12 565
respectively.

Tiie income from this fund is restricted and may be used only to provide
financial assistance to needy children for educational purposes.
Mildred R. Brown and Leroy G. Brown Memorial Fund:
Principal and income from this fund are to be used for making loans
for educational purposes to any children that the Board of Trustees deems
worthy.

Alida O. Meserve Trust Fund:
The principal of this fund is to be used for playgrounds, playground
equipment and other comparable forms of recreation for the children at
Covina.
Relph Walter Kanz and Russell Joseph Kanz Trusts:
lbe principal and income of these trusts shall be used for the
education of the two named beneficiaries, subject to the discretion of
the trustees. When both beneficiaries have completed or abandoned their
education or reached age 27, the trust estate remaining shall be distributed to the Masonic Homes of California.

Frederick E. and Frieda E. Somaers Trust:
Clifton S. Slonaker Annuity Trust Fund:
lbis fund is to be used exclusively for the education of full orphan
children.
George M. and Florence G. Perine Endowment Fund:
lbe principal of this fund, subject to the provision included in the
will of the donor, shall be kept intact and only the income therefrom
shall be used for the benefit of the Union City Home.
Harriet C. Wadleigh Endowment Annuity Fund:
lbis fund, in the orignal amount of $30,000, is subject to a contract
with the donor providing for the payments of certain life annuities out of
the principal and income thereof. Under the terma of the contract, principal of the fund expended in payment of the annuities is to be later restored
out of income when the annuities no longer absorb the entire income. After
restoration of the principal to the original sum of $30,000, the income from
the fund is to be used for the benefit of the residents of the Covina Home.
Student Aid Fund:
lbis fund is designated by the trustees for use as student aid.
Edmund Clement Atkinson Fund:
Tiie principal of this fund, subject to a provision in the will of the
donor, shall be used to contribute to the comfort, convenience and enjoyment of the residents of the Union City Home,

Tiie principal and income of this Fund is held by the Masonic Homes
of California subject to a life annuity.

247 ,074

To insure observance of limitations and restrictions placed on the
use of resources available to the Foundation, the accounts of the Foundation are maintained in accordance with the principles of fund accounting.
'l'he assets, liabilities and fund balances of the Foundation are
reported in two self-balancing funds, as follow:

for support of Foundation operations.
Amaranth Fund - Resources are restricted by a trust agTeement with
the Amaranth Homes of California. 'lhe agTeement specifies that
principal is to be invested and the income is to be used to provide
educational grants to women under age 21.

between reporting periods are ieported as unrealized appreciation or
depreciation in market value of investments.
Investment income is reported when earned.

NJTE 4 - FEDERAL EXCISE TAXES:
In accordance with the applicable provisions of the Ta: Reform Act of
1969, the Foundations is aubject to an excise tax on net investment income,
including realized gains, as defined by the act. Accordingly, federal excise
taxes have been accrued in ainounts of $1,413 and $1,520 aa of June 30, 1980
and 1979, respectively.
In addition, the Tax Reform Act requires that certain minimum distributions be made in accordance with a specified form.ila. At June 30, 1980, the
Foundation had distributed more than the required minimum.

Masonic Homes of California's Pooled Income Fund is a
trust through which donors can make irrevocable gifts
to the Masonic Homes, retaining the income from the
property for themselves or for other living individuals
for life.
All contributions to the Pool are invested together,
and all life beneficiaries receive income based on their
proportionate shares of the Pool. Upon the death of t~e
beneficiaries the gift is withdrawn from the Pool and is
distributed to Masonic Homes of California, a charitable
corporation.
A Pooled Income Fund gift is an irrevocable transfe~ and
affects the donor's entire estate plan and current income
situation. It deserves the most careful consideration.
Donors are urged to consult their own attorneys before
making Pooled Income Fund gifts.
Masonic Homes of California's Pooled Income Fund was
established as a trust under California law on October 15,
1974 by a Declaration of Trust. The Board of Trustees of
the Masonic Homes of California is the Trustee of the
Pooled IQcome Fund and acts in that capacity only so long
as the Beneficiary or Beneficiaries live.
For information purposes, following is an audited statement of the Pooled Income Fund and related statement by
Lindquist, von Husen & Joyce, certified public accountants.

NOTE 1 - ORGANIZATION:
The Masonic Homes Pooled Income Fund was organized on
October 15, 1974 and is a charitable remainder trust to which donors
contribute irrevocable remainder interests in property while retaining
an income interest for life for one or more beneficiaries. The donors
are entitled to a tax deduction equivalent to the present value of the
remainder interest in the property contributed.
The property transferred by such donor is held in trust by the
Board of Trustees of the Masonic Homes Pooled Income· Fund and is co-mingled
with and invested and reinvested with other properties transferred to the
Fund. All income of the Fund is distributed quarterly to the beneficiaries ,
based on their proportionate share of the Pool. Upon the death of each
donor's last income beneficiary, the remainder interest is distributed to
Masonic Homes of california, a charitable corporation.
NOTE 2 - SUMHARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:
Method of Accounting:
The financial statements are prepared on the accrual basis
of accounting.
Investments:
Investments are reported at their fair market value as of
June 30. Properties contributed during the year by donors are recorded
at their fair market value at date of receipt and investments purchased
are recorded at cost. The adjustment to the fund balance required at
year end to report investments at their then fair market value is recorded
as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) in market value of investments.
NOTE 3 - FEDERAL AND STATE INCOHE TAXES:
1h" Fu%ld pays no income tax on income distributed to beneficiaries .
Applicable federal and state income taxes are paid by the beneficiaries on
their share of distributed income. The Fund is taxed only on net short-term
gains from the sale of investments.

The accompanying notes are an integral part of these financial statements.
